q-0400.answer:
Surah Ash-Shu'araa (26) — The Poets · 227 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• If We so willed, We could send down a sign that would force them to believe, but We will not do that because We do not want anyone to believe except by choice.
• I have been sent as a warner, and whoever obeys me and follows me and believes in me, then he belongs to me and I to him, whether he is noble or common, upper-class or lower-class.
• Their chiefs and leaders, who called them to Shirk, disbelief and opposition to the truth.
• They denied the truth that came to them, so they will come to know the news of the consequences of this denial after a while.
• Every time a Scripture comes from heaven to them, most of the people turn away from it.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0475.answer:
Surah Ad-Dukhaan (44) — The Smoke · 59 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Everything that happens and is decreed by Allah and the revelation that He sends down – it all happens by His command, by His leave and with His knowledge.
• They will come to know who will be victorious and whose word will prevail in this world and in the Hereafter.
• By the clear Book,
• Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].
• And the heaven and earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved.

q-0611.answer:
Surah An-Naba (78) — The Announcement · 40 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Refutation against the Idolators' Denial of the Occurrence of the Day of Judgement
• Explaining the Day of Decision and what occurs during it
• The Day of Judgement. It is mentioned here to emphasize the fact that its occurrence has become close, because everything that is coming will certainly come to pass.
• What are they asking about? They are asking about the matter of the Day of Judgement, and it is the great news.
• They used to deny the evidences of Allah and His proofs for His creation, which He revealed to His Messengers.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

Surah Al-Inshiqaaq (84) — The Splitting Open · 25 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Splitting the Heavens asunder and stretching the Earth forth on the Day of Resurrection
• Inform them, O Muhammad, that Allah has prepared for them a painful torment.
• The Recompense for Deeds is True
• From their mannerism is rejection, obstinacy, and opposition to the truth.
• Certainly Allah will repeat his creation just as he began his creation, and He will reward him based upon his deeds, whether they were good or bad.

c-0037.answer:
He doesn't — the Quran says so itself, repeatedly. "O mankind, you are the ones in need of Allah; Allah is the Free-of-need, the Praiseworthy" (35:15). "Whoever is grateful, is grateful only for his own soul's benefit" (31:12); "If you disbelieved — you and everyone on earth together — Allah is still Free of need" (14:8). Worship in Islam was never a supply line to heaven; it is the maintenance schedule of the human being.

Think of what the practices actually do to the one performing them: five daily prayers interrupt heedlessness and reset perspective; fasting installs self-command over the strongest appetites; zakat amputates greed and feeds the poor; gratitude rewires how you experience everything you already have; and remembrance quiets the anxiety of a creature that knows it will die — "Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest" (13:28). A doctor prescribing exercise does not need your push-ups. The real question hiding inside this one is reversed by the Quran: not "why does God need worship?" but "why do humans, in every civilization ever recorded, need to worship — and what were they built for?" (30:30). Worship is not a tax paid to power; it is the soul plugged back into its source.
